history.summary: TOWN CORRECTED: the CSV town 'Durg' here means the Durg-Bhilai urban agglomeration; this Balaji temple stands at Sector 5 / Civic Centre, Bhilai, Durg district — not in Durg city proper. It is a well-known Vaishnavite temple of Bhilai with a long-running official blog (balajimandirbhilai.blogspot.com) documenting its activities; its founding date and history are not published online. Distinct from Shree Salasar Balaji Dham in Raipur (about 43 km away) and from the 1610 Balaji temple of Raigarh district. Coordinates are approximate for the Sector 5/Civic Centre area (verify).

name: Balaji Dham
town_description: Bhilai is the industrial city of Durg district, Chhattisgarh, and the second-largest urban area in the state after Raipur, forming the Durg-Bhilai urban agglomeration with Durg city. It grew around the Bhilai Steel Plant, founded 1955-1959 with Soviet collaboration, and its planned sectors house a culturally diverse population that celebrates Durga Puja, Ganesh Chaturthi, Ugadi, Pongal and Eid side by side.
